newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Brazzaville firing delays mediation statement.
newsitem.headline: Brazzaville firing delays mediation statement.

text.p: Renewed shelling in the Congolese capital on Saturday delayed a scheduled statement on progress made towards a resolution of the conflict raging in Brazzaville.
A spokesman for Bernard Kolelas, the city's mayor and the president of a national mediation committee, said the statement could not be released amid the sound of shelling.
Brazzaville residents attributed the shelling to regular troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba attacking the once thriving -- and now deserted -- market districts of Poto-Poto and Moungali.
Hellot Mampouya, another Kolelas spokesman, said Kolelas was still expected to make an announcement on Saturday.

The conflict between Lissouba and his predecessor and rival Denis Sassou Nguesso has now gone on for more than a month. It has left hundreds of people dead, tens of thousands displaced and whole districts of the normally sleepy Congolese capital devastated.
